title: The Rhythm the Drug Could Break — Dofetilide (Tikosyn) Inpatient QT Gate, Human hERG Cryo-EM Cavity (PDB 5VA2), Reverse Use-Dependence, Renal OCT2/MATE1 & the DIAMOND Trials

teenKit.tldr: Dofetilide is a powerful heart medication that successfully cures chaotic rhythms, but ironically sets a microscopic trap that can cause fatal electrical chaos at slow heart rates. To prevent disaster, patients must take their first doses in a hospital while doctors constantly monitor their heart's electrical timing.
teenKit.whyItMatters: This drug proves that in modern medicine, the line between a life-saving cure and a lethal weapon often comes down to the nanometer-scale architecture of a single protein channel.
keyTakeaways: Dofetilide works by blocking potassium channels in the heart, specifically targeting the human hERG channel to reset erratic heartbeats like atrial fibrillation.
Reverse use-dependence means the drug becomes dangerously more potent when the heart beats slowly, turning a resting pulse into a high-risk electrical hazard.
Structural biology using cryo-electron microscopy reveals that drug molecules physically wedge themselves into the tiny amino acid cavity (Tyr652/Phe656) of the ion pore.

vocab.meaning: A microscopic protein tunnel in heart cells that lets potassium flow out to reset the heart's electrical charge after every beat.
A terrifying pharmacological quirk where a drug's dangerous side effects actually increase when the heart rate slows down.
A high-tech imaging technique that freezes biological molecules to take crystal-clear pictures of them down to the individual atom.
A common heart condition where the upper chambers quiver chaotically instead of beating in a clean, coordinated rhythm.

quiz.question: Why must patients stay in the hospital for three mandatory days just to start taking dofetilide?
options: To build up their muscle mass before exercising
To monitor their heart's electrical timing as the drug triggers its dangerous trap
Because the pills are too expensive to take at home
To test their blood type daily
quiz.explanation: Doctors must closely watch the heart's electrical intervals in a controlled setting because the drug can suddenly cause fatal heart rhythms.

quiz.question: What does 'reverse use-dependence' mean in the context of dofetilide?
options: The drug works better the faster you run
The drug is stronger when the heart beats slowly
The drug stops working entirely after three days
The drug only works if you take it backwards
quiz.explanation: Unlike most drugs that get stronger with high activity, dofetilide's blocking effect becomes dangerously intense when the heart rate drops.

quiz.question: What technological breakthrough allowed scientists to see how dofetilide physically traps itself in the heart channel?
quiz.explanation: Cryo-EM imaging provides atomic-level detail of the Kv11.1 channel, showing precisely where drug molecules wedge into the pore.
